title: Broker system-integration terms
summary: Open a multi-system integration, negotiate exact opaque Markdown terms bilaterally with versioned steward scopes, seal current unanimous agreements, and review their composition or later implementation conformance without changing target systems.
use_when: A proposed entrant has explicit expectations of one or more existing systems and each system steward should reconcile those expectations with its exact implementation and contracts.
Several independently owned systems of concern must reach visible bilateral terms before a design proceeds.
A sealed design agreement needs an explicit successor amendment or an evidence-only review against a supplied candidate implementation basis.
do_not_use_when: The caller only needs to inspect or export an existing Pratica record; use pratica.agreement.explore.
The request is to discover every relevant system automatically, implement CRM or another product, mutate a stewarded system, deploy, release, or enforce terms at runtime.
The entrant cannot yet state complete Markdown expectations or the target basis cannot be supplied through an authorized source boundary.
outcome: One or more immutable bilateral agreements in which every fixed party assents to the same exact current Markdown offer on the recorded steward basis, optionally accompanied by a separate immutable composition or conformance review.
effects: Writes private Pratica SQLite integrations, tracks, negotiations, offers, assents, agreements, source snapshots, attempts, and reviews.
Steward response, composition review, and conformance review submit one-attempt Nucleus jobs using Codex and can consume account allowance.
Managed source tools disclose only the frozen bounded source snapshots selected for that attempt to Nucleus and Codex.
No command changes target-system source, contracts, database, service, deployment, release, or authorization state.
authority: Entrant and steward parties author and assent to complete offers; Pratica owns offer order, currentness, assent, basis guards, seals, attempts, reviews, and domain success.
Each target system remains authoritative for its implementation and current behavioral contracts; a steward response is scoped to the exact recorded basis.
Nucleus owns admission, authentication, agent execution, job history, and its durable tool mailbox but never decides agreement, retry, or implementation success.
success: Each agreement seals only while its negotiation head, complete required-party assent set, and exact steward basis remain current.
Every accepted model-assisted outcome is a validated immutable Pratica tool call committed to Pratica state; Nucleus completion or final prose alone is insufficient.
A composition review names the exact agreement set and remains advisory; a conformance review names one sealed agreement and one frozen candidate basis and remains evidence-only.
The integration report states selected coverage and unresolved findings without claiming exhaustive system discovery or implementation proof.
failure_and_recovery: A stale offer or basis rejects the proposed transition without a partial write; inspect current state and open a deliberate successor offer or attempt.
Ambiguous Nucleus admission repeats only the exact persisted request under the same job ID; a new attempt requires explicit retry and a new job identity.
A committed Pratica domain result remains authoritative if the harness later fails; do not repeat it from terminal runtime state.
A Nucleus restart makes an unfinished Codex attempt lost and does not authorize automatic retry or direct-Codex fallback.
privacy: Terms, source snapshots, prompts, citations, reviews, and exports can contain private implementation and product-design material in both Pratica and Nucleus state.
Use private input paths and isolated state where appropriate; release bundles, fixtures, Chancery, and logs must contain no real negotiated contract or source body.

interfaces.label: Open bilateral track
interfaces.invocation: /Users/joey/.local/bin/pratica track open INTEGRATION --steward SCOPE [--steward-version VERSION] --terms FILE

does_not_authorize: Changing, implementing, testing, migrating, deploying, or releasing CRM or another target system.
Treating a steward response as authority beyond its selected scope and basis, or a review as party assent or integration approval.
Retrying a terminal attempt, publishing private terms, or accepting target-system changes without separate explicit authority.
